# DeepSeek-V4-Flash on RTP-LLM

Adaptation of DeepSeek-V4-Flash (154.5B, MoE with mHC + CSA/HCA/SWA
attention, native FP4/FP8 weights) for the RTP-LLM inference engine.

## Status snapshot (2026-04-26)

**Single-card correctness** ✅
- End-to-end generation through `NormalEngine` + `PyWrappedModel`
  producing correct chat completions on a single SM100_ARM (189 GB HBM)
  GPU. Gated by bazel smoke
  `//internal_source/rtp_llm/test/smoke:v4_flash_native_fp4_fp8_tp1_sm100`
  (~155-230 s depending on cache, both prompts bit-exact golden match).

**Kernel migration S1–S7-prep** ✅ (kernel_audit.md K1–K10, K14–K17
addressed; K5/K11/K12/K13 explicitly kept REF)
- Attention / Indexer / shared-expert FP8 linears — `CudaFp8DeepGEMMLinear`
  via `LinearFactory`. (S2/S3)
- **Routed-expert FP4 path — `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_gemm_nt` per expert**
  (2026-04-26). Matches V4-official `Linear.forward`; grouped GEMM
  deliberately NOT used (V4-official doesn't use it either, and our
  grouped wrapper had a latent alignment bug the synthetic equivalence
  test couldn't catch).
- Sparse attention — V4's own TileLang `sparse_attn_kernel`, vendored
  from `inference/kernel.py`. (S5)
- deep_gemm bumped to **upstream 2.5.0** (commit `891d57b`, 2026-04-24),
  built locally for aarch64 cu129, uploaded to OSS, wired through
  `internal_source/deps/requirements_cuda12_arm.txt`.

**MTPBlock speculative-decode head** ✅ plumbing ready (2026-04-26)
- Full Python port in `block.py::MTPBlock`. Extends `Block` with
  `e_proj`/`h_proj` (FP8 via factory or `QuantizedLinear`), three extra
  RMSNorms (`enorm`, `hnorm`, `norm`), and per-layer `hc_head_fn/base/scale`.
  `forward_draft(x, start_pos, input_ids, embed, lm_head_weight)` returns
  `[B, S, vocab]` logits.
- Wired into `V4Transformer` via `_build_mtp_block` — activates when
  `n_mtp_layers > 0`. `DeepSeekV4Model` still pins `n_mtp_layers=0`
  because the framework-side speculative-decode driver (`SpeculativeConfig`,
  draft sampler, extra-layer KV cache budget) is a separate effort.
- Unit test: `dsv4/test/mtp_block_test.py`.
- Latent-bug fix bundled in: `Expert._apply(self, layer, x)` shadowed
  `nn.Module._apply(fn)` and silently broke `.to(device, dtype)`. Renamed
  to `_apply_layer`.

**Parallelism** 🟡 partial
- **S7-prep**: `ParallelismConfig` threaded into `V4Args`. ✅
- **S7c (DP=4 + EP=4)** ✅ (2026-04-26): Config B — attention DP /
  expert EP. Smoke `v4_flash_dp4_ep4_sm100` green in 121.7 s, both
  golden prompts bit-exact. Weight loader filters routed experts to
  64 per rank (HBM 150 GB → 50 GB per rank); `MoE.forward` calls
  `DeepEPWrapper.buffer.dispatch/combine` around the per-expert FP4
  loop. Bring-up at `max_seq_len=8K`; raising past 32K waits on the
  K9 Indexer TileLang kernel. See `parallel_design.md` S7c and
  `gotchas.md` §§17–23 for the seven non-obvious bugs hit.
- **S7a (TP=4 attention)** — scaffold landed but output diverges from
  golden (4 ranked hypotheses in `parallel_design.md`). **Deferred**
  in favor of DP+EP; may not be needed since V4-official decode also
  prefers the DP+EP pattern.
- **S7b (TP+EP)** — not started; would build on S7a.
- **S7d (DeepEP LL router)** — not started; lands after S7c stable
  at larger contexts.

**Framework-level** ⏳ not started
- M4 heterogeneous KV cache pool (CSA/HCA/SWA have different shapes).
- PD disagg (blocked on M4).
- Decode CUDA graph (blocked on M4 + graph-safe `reset_rope_cache`).
- MTPBlock driver (framework-side, not model-side).

### `TF_CUDA_VERSION` pin — 13.0 vs 13.2

`3rdparty/cuda_config/find_cuda_config.py` asserts that `cuda.h`'s
`CUDA_VERSION` macro matches `TF_CUDA_VERSION` at the major.minor
level. CUDA 13.2 installs `/usr/local/cuda-13.2/include/cuda.h` with
`#define CUDA_VERSION 13020`. If you bump the toolkit but forget this
pin, the very first repo-rule fetch fails with:

```
Could not find any cuda.h matching version '13.0' in any subdirectory
```

Always bump `.bazelrc` in lockstep with the toolkit. Current pin:

```
build:cuda13_base --action_env TF_CUDA_VERSION="13.2"
build:cuda13_base --host_action_env TF_CUDA_VERSION="13.2"
build:cuda13_base --repo_env=TF_CUDA_VERSION=13.2
```

**Why a separate repo and not patches conditional at build time?**
Bazel's `new_git_repository` doesn't support conditional patches, and
CUDA-13-patched sources would break the CUDA-12 build. Cloning the
repo twice (with different `name=`) is the clean way to keep both

### 1. CUDA 13.2.1 toolkit via rpm network repo

CUDA 13.2 is **only** distributed through the rpm network repo — NVIDIA
does not ship a `.run` local installer or a `cuda-repo-rhel8-13-2-local`
tarball for it. So the install changed from:

```dockerfile
# CUDA 12.9 / 13.0 — .run installer
wget .../cuda_13.0.2_580.95.05_linux_sbsa.run -O 1.run && \
    sh 1.run --silent --toolkit
```

to:

```dockerfile
# CUDA 13.2 — network repo
RUN curl -fsSL https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/rhel8/sbsa/D42D0685.pub -o /tmp/cuda.pub && \
    rpm --import /tmp/cuda.pub && \
    rm -f /tmp/cuda.pub && \
    curl -fsSL https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/rhel8/sbsa/cuda-rhel8.repo \
        -o /etc/yum.repos.d/cuda-rhel8-sbsa.repo && \
    dnf install -y --setopt=install_weak_deps=False cuda-toolkit-13-2-13.2.1-1 && \
    dnf clean all && \
    rm -f /etc/yum.repos.d/cuda-rhel8-sbsa.repo && \
    ln -sfn /usr/local/cuda-13.2 /usr/local/cuda
```

Notes:
- `cuda-toolkit-13-2-13.2.1-1` is the meta-package: toolkit components
  only, **no** driver — the driver stays on the host (580.95.05).
- `--setopt=install_weak_deps=False` prevents dnf from pulling in
  recommended-but-optional packages like `nsight-compute-*` which
  inflate the image significantly.
- The repo file is removed after install to keep the image reproducible
  and avoid future `dnf update` surprises.
- `ln -sfn /usr/local/cuda-13.2 /usr/local/cuda` — network-repo installs
  go to `/usr/local/cuda-13.2/` whereas the old `.run` installer
  wrote to `/usr/local/cuda/`. All other pieces of the Dockerfile and
  bazel config assume `/usr/local/cuda`, so we create the symlink.

### 4. CCCL header symlinks (unchanged from 13.0 work)

CUDA 13 ships CCCL headers (`cub/`, `cuda/`, `cuda/std/`, `libcudacxx/`,

## Failure mode hit during build — `rpm --import -` under qemu-arm64

### Symptom

First pipeline attempt (`run 38200373`) failed in 4 min at step
`image-os-gpu-cuda13-arm`:

```
#8 [ 4/18] RUN curl -fsSL ...D42D0685.pub | rpm --import - && ...
#8 0.266 error: -: import read failed(0).
#8 6.031 (23) Failed writing body
```

### Diagnosis

The Aone buildkit runs aarch64 builds on x86_64 builders by invoking
`buildkit_qemu_emulator` for each `RUN` step. Stdin piping between two
emulated processes (`curl` → `rpm --import -`) is unreliable: `rpm`
reads 0 bytes from stdin before curl has flushed any. rpm errors
quickly; curl sees the broken pipe as "Failed writing body (23)".

This is consistent with [docker-buildx issue #1570](https://github.com/docker/buildx/issues/1570)
on qemu-user cross-arch builds: pipe buffering is not emulated
consistently.

### Fix (commit `5899739292`)

Download the GPG key to a file first and import from the file. No
pipe-emulation risk:

```diff
-RUN curl -fsSL ...D42D0685.pub | rpm --import - && \
+RUN curl -fsSL ...D42D0685.pub -o /tmp/cuda.pub && \
+    rpm --import /tmp/cuda.pub && \
+    rm -f /tmp/cuda.pub && \
     curl -fsSL ...cuda-rhel8.repo -o /etc/yum.repos.d/cuda-rhel8-sbsa.repo && \
     dnf install -y ...
```

Second pipeline run (`run 38200783`) completed in 33m52s — full success.

General rule for anything running through the ARM-on-x86 buildkit:
**avoid shell pipes between separate binaries in `RUN` steps**.
Stage to a file, then consume. Applies to `curl | tar`, `wget | sha256sum`,
`cat | cmd`, etc.

# Kernel Linkage Under nvcc 13 — The Central CUDA 13 Issue

The one structural change in nvcc from 12 → 13 that actually breaks the
existing RTP-LLM codebase: **`__global__` template instantiations are
now emitted with internal / local linkage**. Cross-TU references to
their kernel addresses — which were common in the codebase for
`cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor()` calls and for
`kernel<<<>>>` launches from an `#include`d template header — no
longer resolve at link time.

## The symptom

When loading `librtp_compute_ops.so` (BIND_NOW / RTLD_NOW), dlopen
fails with something like:

```
ImportError: .../librtp_compute_ops.so: undefined symbol:
_ZN10flashinfer33BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernelILNS_15PosEncodingModeE0ELj2ELj1ELj16ELj16ELj3ELj2E
   NS_16DefaultAttentionILb0ELb1ELb1ELb0EEENS_17BatchDecodeParamsI6__half13__nv_fp8_e4m3S5_iEEEEvT7_
```

or the analogous:

```
undefined symbol: _ZN12tensorrt_llm7kernels14addCumLogProbsIfEE...
```

## The root cause — Itanium-ABI `L`-prefix mangling

nvcc 13 emits explicit template instantiations of `__global__` kernels
with the Itanium **`L`-prefix** on the mangled name, which denotes
**local linkage** (the symbol is not exported from its TU). Compare
what `nm` shows for the same kernel between CUDA 12 and CUDA 13:

```
# CUDA 12 output — external weak symbol, caller and definer both
# generate the SAME mangled name:
$ nm --demangle libflashinfer_batch_paged_decode_256.so | grep BatchDecodeWith
W  _ZN10flashinfer33BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel... flashinfer::BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel<...>

# CUDA 13 output — local symbol with an L-prefix inside the namespace
# mangling; the caller's request (no L-prefix) can't match:
$ nm --demangle libflashinfer_batch_paged_decode_256.so | grep BatchDecodeWith
t  _ZN10flashinferL33BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel... flashinfer::BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel<...>
```

Note the `W` (weak external) → `t` (local text) flag change **and**
the extra `L` character after the namespace-name length prefix.
Because the mangled names differ textually, a caller TU that requests
`_ZN10flashinfer33...` will never resolve to a symbol defined as
`_ZN10flashinferL33...`, even inside the same shared library.

### When does this actually break?

Any place where:

1. A `__global__` template kernel is defined in one TU, and
2. Another TU takes the kernel's address or invokes `<<<>>>` by
   including a template header that expands the launch,
3. While both TUs are compiled with nvcc 13.

`cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&n, kernel, ...)` is
the canonical offender — it literally takes the kernel's address
across TU boundaries. `<<<>>>` launches from an included template
header are the same thing under the hood (nvcc rewrites them into a
call to `cudaLaunchKernel(&kernel, ...)`).

### Doesn't cc_library-vs-cc_shared_library solve this?

No. The `L`-prefix lives in the **mangled name itself**, so the caller
and definer reference different-named symbols even when linked into
the same static archive. Making them part of one cc_library doesn't
produce a match; the caller still asks for the un-prefixed name.

Only fixes:
- Put the kernel launch / kernel address-taking into the **same TU**
  as the kernel definition (the host-wrapper approach).
- Or remove the cross-TU dependency entirely (skip the cudaOccupancy
  call, hard-code a reasonable value).

## Fix 1 — flashinfer cudaOccupancy skip

**Patch:** `github-opensource/3rdparty/flashinfer/0015-cuda13-occupancy-skip.patch`

**Target:** `include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh` — three
`WorkEstimation` functions that take kernel addresses for occupancy
queries:
- `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel` (plain MHA decode)
- `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernelMLA` (MLA variant)
- `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernelMlaCuteSM80` (CuTe SM80 MLA)

**Shape of the change (one of the three hunks):**

```diff
-    auto kernel =
-        BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheKernel<POS_ENCODING_MODE, NUM_STAGES_SMEM, tile_size_per_bdx,
-                                          vec_size, bdx, bdy, bdz, AttentionVariant, Params>;
-    int num_blocks_per_sm = 0;
+    (void)num_threads;
+    (void)smem_size;
+    // CUDA 13 nvcc emits __global__ template instantiations with local/internal
+    // linkage (Itanium L-prefix mangling), so taking the kernel's address from
+    // another TU (e.g. batch_decode.cu vs batch_paged_decode_*.cu) fails to
+    // resolve at link time. Skip cudaOccupancy and use a conservative heuristic;
+    // only affects the split_kv decision, not correctness.
+    int num_blocks_per_sm = 2;
     int num_sm = 0;
     int dev_id = 0;
     FLASHINFER_CUDA_CALL(cudaGetDevice(&dev_id));
     FLASHINFER_CUDA_CALL(cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&num_sm, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev_id));
-    FLASHINFER_CUDA_CALL(cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&num_blocks_per_sm, kernel,
-                                                                       num_threads, smem_size));
     max_grid_size = num_blocks_per_sm * num_sm;
```

**Effect:** `num_blocks_per_sm` is hard-coded to 2 rather than
queried from the runtime. This feeds into the `split_kv` heuristic:
`max_grid_size = num_blocks_per_sm * num_sm`; `split_kv` is set to
`false` when `batch_size * gdy >= max_grid_size`. In practice this is
a perf heuristic only — correctness is unaffected.

**Format gotcha:** the patch must use `--- include/...` headers (no
`a/` / `b/` prefix) to match the format of the existing
`0001..0010` flashinfer patches. `git diff` output with `a/` / `b/`
prefixes must be stripped via `sed -e 's|^--- a/|--- |' -e 's|^+++ b/|+++ |'`.

## Fix 2 — beamSearchKernels host-wrapper refactor

**Files:**
- `github-opensource/3rdparty/trt_beam_search/beamSearchKernels.h` — declare wrapper
- `github-opensource/3rdparty/trt_beam_search/beamSearchKernels.cu` — define wrapper + kernel
- `github-opensource/3rdparty/trt_beam_search/beamSearchKernelsTemplate.h` — call wrapper instead of `<<<>>>`

**Problem:** the old pattern:

```cpp
// beamSearchKernels.cu — defines and instantiates
template <typename T>
__global__ void addCumLogProbs(T* ..., ...) { ... }

template __global__ void addCumLogProbs<float>(...);
template __global__ void addCumLogProbs<half>(...);
```

```cpp
// beamSearchKernelsTemplate.h — #include'd by beamSearchKernels{4,8,16,...}.cu
template <typename T, int PBM>
void beamSearchKernelLauncher(...)
{
    ...
    addCumLogProbs<<<nBS, nThread, 0, stream>>>(...);  // cross-TU launch
    ...
}
```

Under nvcc 13 the `addCumLogProbs<float>` instantiation in
`beamSearchKernels.cu.o` gets the `L`-prefix, but the caller in
`beamSearchKernels16.cu.o` requests the non-prefixed name → undefined
symbol at link.

**Fix:** move the launch into the same TU as the kernel definition,
expose a host wrapper:

```cpp
// beamSearchKernels.cu — kernel moved into anonymous namespace
namespace {
template <typename T>
__global__ void addCumLogProbsKernel(T* ..., ...) { ... }
} // namespace

// Host wrapper, same TU as kernel definition:
template <typename T>
void launchAddCumLogProbs(T* pStage1LogProbs, ..., int nThread, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    addCumLogProbsKernel<T><<<nBS, nThread, 0, stream>>>(
        pStage1LogProbs, cumLogProbs, finished, endIds, diversityRates,
        batchSlots, nBS, nBMIn, nBMOut);
    check_cuda_error();
}

// Explicit instantiation of the WRAPPER (ordinary function, external linkage):
template void launchAddCumLogProbs<float>(...);
template void launchAddCumLogProbs<half>(...);
```

```cpp
// beamSearchKernels.h — declare wrapper
template <typename T>
void launchAddCumLogProbs(
    T* pStage1LogProbs, float const* cumLogProbs, FinishedState const* finished,
    int const* endIds, float const* diversityRates,
    runtime::SizeType32 const* batchSlots, size_t nBS, size_t nBMIn, size_t nBMOut,
    int nThread, cudaStream_t stream);
```

```cpp
// beamSearchKernelsTemplate.h — call wrapper, no more <<<>>>
launchAddCumLogProbs<T>(pStage1LogProbs, bh.cumLogProbsIn, bh.finished, bh.endIds,
                        bh.diversityRates, bh.batchSlots, nBS, nBMIn, nBMOut,
                        nThread, stream);
```

Why this works: the wrapper is an ordinary (non-`__global__`)
function. Its template instantiation obeys standard Itanium ABI, no
`L` prefix, external linkage, resolves cleanly cross-TU. The `<<<>>>`
launch (which under the hood takes the kernel's address) happens
inside the wrapper, same TU as the kernel definition — address
resolves locally within the TU.

## Fix 3 — CUB API removals (`3rdparty/cub_compat.h`)

Not a linkage issue; a separate CUDA 13 source-compat issue. Mentioned
here because the consumers overlap with the trt_beam_search and
flashinfer changes above.

CUDA 13 CUB dropped:
- `cub::Max` / `cub::Min` / `cub::Sum` (use `cuda::maximum<T>{}` / etc.)
- `cub::CountingInputIterator` (moved namespace)
- `cub::TransformInputIterator` (moved namespace)

Our `3rdparty/cub_compat.h` provides a small backward-compat header
that aliases the old names to the new ones on CUDA 13 and is a no-op
on CUDA 12.

Consumers (add `#include "3rdparty/cub_compat.h"` and depend on
`//3rdparty:cub_compat` in BUILD):

- `3rdparty/flashinfer/0011-cuda13-cub-compat.patch` — patched into
  flashinfer's `sampling.cuh`
- `3rdparty/trt_beam_search/topkLastDim.cu`
- `rtp_llm/models_py/bindings/common/kernels/moe/moe_routing_kernels.cu`

## Non-fixes — things that looked plausible but didn't help

- **`0013` / `0014` visibility patches** (`__attribute__((visibility("default")))`
  on flashinfer kernel decls/defs) — kept in the tree but don't fix
  linkage on their own. Visibility controls whether the symbol is
  exported from the shared library; it doesn't change the mangled
  name. Since the `L`-prefix is in the mangled name, visibility is
  orthogonal. Patches left in as harmless.
- **Merging flashinfer BUILD into a single cc_library** — was
  considered to avoid the split. Tested; doesn't help. See the
  "Doesn't cc_library-vs-cc_shared_library solve this?" section above.
- **Bumping flashinfer upstream commit** — upstream has CUDA-13
  adaptations but requires a major JIT refactor in our BUILD file.
  Out of scope.

## Diagnostics commands

To confirm whether a given `undefined symbol` is the L-prefix issue,
grep the defining object for the mangled name **with and without** the
`L`:

```bash
# Suppose the error is:
#   undefined symbol: _ZN12tensorrt_llm7kernels14addCumLogProbsIfEE...
#
# 1. Confirm the symbol isn't in the .o / .a / .so:
nm --demangle .../beamSearchKernels.cu.o | grep -F addCumLogProbs
#   → shows _ZN12tensorrt_llmL7kernels14addCumLogProbs... (note the `L`)
#
# 2. Check if the caller requests the L form or the non-L form:
nm -u --demangle .../beamSearchKernels16.cu.o | grep addCumLogProbs
#   → shows _ZN12tensorrt_llm7kernels14addCumLogProbs... (no `L`)
#
# The textual mismatch (`L` vs no-`L`) is the telltale.
```

If the error looks like this — cross-TU template kernel, caller and
definer have mangled names that differ only in an `L` — the fix is
either Fix 1 (skip the cudaOccupancy call) or Fix 2 (host wrapper in
same TU as the kernel). Don't try to change visibility or rearrange
BUILD targets.

## Common failure modes

### `fatal: Could not read from remote repository`

Running as the wrong uid / `$HOME` in the container. See step 4.
Quick check: `pouch exec -u wangyin.yx wangyin_cuda132 id` should
print `uid=1337565`. If not, `/etc/passwd` needs its `wangyin.yx`
home dir fixed — must be `/home/admin/wangyin.yx`, not `/home/wangyin`.

### `Could not find any cuda.h matching version '13.0'`

`.bazelrc` `TF_CUDA_VERSION` still pinned to 13.0 but the toolkit
is 13.2. Update to `13.2` (see `build_config.md`).

### `undefined symbol: _ZN...` during dlopen

Cross-TU local-linkage kernel reference slipped through — some new
CUDA code either added a `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor`
call that takes a `__global__` template kernel's address from a
different TU, or added a `<<<>>>` launch in an `#include`d template
header whose kernel is defined elsewhere. See `kernel_linkage.md`
for diagnosis and fix patterns.

### `No space left on device` mounting /home inside pouch cp

/home/admin is 100% full. Use the staging-to-`/tmp` pattern in
step 3 instead of `pouch cp`.

### `Repo id must be in the form 'repo_name' or 'namespace/repo_name': '/mnt/nas1/hf/...'`

Model weights not present at the expected path; HF hub tries to parse
the local path as a repo id. See step 7.

### `start frontend server error: ...` early in the test log

Usually a test-infra issue, not a CUDA 13.2 regression. Check the
first few ERROR lines for the actual cause (most commonly: model
weights missing, renderer import error, port already in use).

Where the DeepSeek-V4 smoke stands on CUDA 13.2. **Status: PASSED byte-for-byte
against a regenerated golden (2026-04-26).** This document retains the
investigation history that led to the golden refresh so the *why* is
recorded.

## Target under test

```
//internal_source/rtp_llm/test/smoke:v4_flash_native_fp4_fp8_tp1_sm100
```

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (~150 GB BF16, native FP4/FP8 weights)

Golden: `internal_source/rtp_llm/test/smoke/data/model/deepseek_v4/q_r_v4_flash_sm100_arm.json`

3. **Runtime correctness:** both queries return **semantically

4. **V4 renderer path:** `DeepseekV4Renderer` now registered (previous

## Current golden (post-refresh, 2026-04-26)

### Query 0 — `"What is the capital of France?"`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `content` | `The capital of France is Paris.` |
| `prompt_tokens` | 11 |

The `prompt_tokens` values include the trailing `</think>` CoT-suppression

### Prior drift (before refresh)

Earlier runs showed `prompt_tokens` exactly +1 higher than the then-golden
(10 → 11, 7 → 8) with different completion content (`**Paris**.` vs
`Paris.`, `4` vs `2 + 2 = 4`). Root cause: the stale golden was captured
when the V4 renderer was commented out and the BasicRenderer fallback was
in play. See the renderer investigation trail below.

## Why this is **not** a CUDA 13.2 issue

### 1. Identical behavior on CUDA 13.0

The same smoke exhibited the same kind of drift (chat-template-related
token offsets, semantically-correct answers) when run on the prior
CUDA 13.0 rebuild. The drift does not correlate with toolkit version.

### 2. The template logic lives in Python

`rtp_llm/openai/renderers/` is plain Python — the bytes placed into
the model's prompt tensor are deterministic and independent of nvcc.
Any CUDA-version regression would show up in the model's generation
(different logits → different tokens), not in how many prompt tokens
are counted.

### 3. The drift is a template-selection bug, not a generation bug

See the renderer trace below — the 1-token offset comes from the V4
renderer's BOS/EOS handling differing by exactly one token from
whatever generated the golden, not from any runtime numerical
difference.

## Renderer investigation trail (how we got here)

### First observation — much larger drift, with `<|im_end` leakage

Initial run (with V4 renderer registration **commented out** in
`rtp_llm/openai/renderers/__init__.py:9`):

```
Expected: "The capital of France is **Paris**.", prompt_tokens=10
Actual  : "The capital of France is Paris.<|im_end", prompt_tokens=30
```

`<|im_end` (truncated by `max_tokens=10` before the closing `|>`) is a
**Qwen ChatML** stop token — never part of DeepSeek's native
special-token set (which uses `<｜User｜>` / `<｜Assistant｜>` /
`<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` instead). This immediately ruled out a V4
model-side bug and pointed at the renderer.

### Renderer-resolution trace

1. `ChatRendererFactory.get_renderer(model_type="deepseek_v4")` — no
   registration exists because `DeepseekV4Renderer`'s import is
   commented out in `renderers/__init__.py` (so
   `register_renderer("deepseek_v4", DeepseekV4Renderer)` in the
   module body never executes).
2. Factory falls back to `BasicRenderer`.
3. `BasicRenderer._setup_chat_template()` tries to load
   `chat_template.jinja` from the ckpt dir — absent.
4. Tries `tokenizer.default_chat_template` — absent (the V4 checkpoint's
   `tokenizer_config.json` has no `chat_template` field).
5. Falls through to the module-level `DEFAULT_CHAT_API_TEMPLATE` in
   `basic_renderer.py:23`, which is Qwen-style ChatML:

   ```python
   DEFAULT_CHAT_API_TEMPLATE = (
       "{% for message in messages %}"
       "{{'<|im_start|>' + message['role'] + '\n' + message['content'] + '<|im_end|>' + '\n'}}"
       "{% endfor %}"
       "{% if add_generation_prompt %}"
       "{{ '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}"
       "{% endif %}"
   )
   ```

6. `add_extra_stop_words(["<|im_end|>"])` — adds a stop word that,
   when the template is misapplied, is present in the output because
   the model has actually learned `<|im_end|>` during SFT on some
   mixed data, so it emits it on its own. With `max_tokens=10` it
   gets truncated mid-token.

The commit that introduced this fallback — `fc56fa411` "feat: add
DeepSeek-V4 OpenAI chat renderer and function-call detector" — says
in its body:

> The renderer is currently registered-but-commented in
> rtp_llm/openai/renderers/__init__.py — during bring-up backend HTTP
> /v1/chat/completions SIGSEGVs inside ChatService::chatCompletions
> when any custom V4 renderer is loaded, so we fall back to
> BasicRenderer via chat_template.jinja in the ckpt dir

So:
- At **golden-generation time** (commit `11bbc2e6c`, 5 min later) a
  `chat_template.jinja` existed in the ckpt dir that gave
  `prompt_tokens=10`. It has since been removed from the ckpt.
- Now both the jinja and the V4 renderer are absent, so it falls all
  the way through to ChatML.

### Fix — re-enable the V4 renderer

```diff

-# Temporarily disabled to debug ChatService crash — fallback to BasicRenderer via chat_template.jinja
-# from .deepseekv4_renderer import DeepseekV4Renderer
+from .deepseekv4_renderer import DeepseekV4Renderer
```

Re-run result: **no SIGSEGV** (whatever the original crash was, it's
no longer reproducible on this build), output now uses the native V4
tokens, and `prompt_tokens` drops from ~30 to ~11 / 8 — within
1 token of golden.

The V4 renderer delegates prompt assembly to the checkpoint's
`encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` script, which uses DeepSeek-native tokens:

```
bos_token          = "<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>"
USER_SP_TOKEN      = "<｜User｜>"
ASSISTANT_SP_TOKEN = "<｜Assistant｜>"
```

## Root cause of the 1-token drift (investigated 2026-04-26)

**The +1 is `</think>` (token id `128822`), not BOS.**

`DeepseekV4Renderer._build_prompt` delegates to the checkpoint's
`encoding/encoding_dsv4.py → render_message()`, which — when called
with the renderer's hard-coded defaults `thinking_mode="chat"` +
`drop_thinking=True` — textually appends `</think>` right after
`<｜Assistant｜>`. This is DeepSeek's documented trick for suppressing
CoT output in chat mode (pre-close the `<think>` block so the model
skips reasoning and goes straight to the answer).

### Token-by-token proof for Query 0 (`"What is the capital of France?"`)

Current V4-renderer prompt — 11 tokens:

```
[0]  0       '<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>'
[1]  128803  '<｜User｜>'
[2]  3085    'What'
[3]  344     ' is'
[4]  270     ' the'
[5]  6102    ' capital'
[6]  294     ' of'
[7]  8760    ' France'
[8]  33      '?'
[9]  128804  '<｜Assistant｜>'
[10] 128822  '</think>'        ← extra token vs golden
```

Golden prompt — 10 tokens. Just drop index [10].

Same pattern on Query 1 (`"2+2="`): current 8 tokens ending in
`<｜Assistant｜></think>`, golden 7 tokens ending in
`<｜Assistant｜>`.

Earlier background hypothesis of a double-BOS was **wrong** — the
checkpoint's `tokenizer_config.json` has `add_bos_token: false`, so
the tokenizer does not auto-prepend BOS. The sole BOS comes from
`encoding_dsv4.py` textually emitting `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` at
prompt start.

### Where the extra token is emitted

`encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` ~L384–392 (in `render_message`), paraphrased:

```python
elif messages[index].get("role") in ["user", "developer"]:
    prompt += ASSISTANT_SP_TOKEN              # "<｜Assistant｜>"
    ...
    if thinking_mode == "chat" and drop_thinking:
        prompt += thinking_end_token          # "</think>" — this is the +1
```

`deepseekv4_renderer.py` sets both of those kwargs as defaults, so
every V4 chat render includes the trailing `</think>`.

### Why the golden doesn't have it

Golden was generated on 2026-04-25 14:35 (commit `11bbc2e6c`), five
minutes after the renderer was added-but-commented-out (commit
`fc56fa411`). At that time the fallback path was BasicRenderer loading
a `chat_template.jinja` from the ckpt dir that emitted just
`<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜User｜>...<｜Assistant｜>` with no trailing
`</think>`. That jinja file has since been removed from the
checkpoint, so we can't verify it directly — but the token count and
semantic output match this theory exactly.

correct** and matches what the checkpoint authors ship in

(non-thinking) mode. The stale golden was refreshed against it:

```python
    rendered_result.rendered_prompt = rendered_result.rendered_prompt[:-len("</think>")]
```

…would fight the encoding script's intent and change generation behavior
(the model emits CoT again without the pre-closed think block). Not done.

## Collateral: why the completions also differ

- **Query 1 went from `"4"` (2 tokens) to `"2 + 2 = 4"` (8 tokens):**
  the trailing `</think>` primes the model for a short formal answer
  that restates the problem before solving; without it, the model just
  dumped the answer. Different prompt → different (both valid) continuation.
- **Query 0 lost the markdown `**Paris**`:** same reason. Temperature=0
  decoding is deterministic per prompt, not across prompts.

Neither is a bug — they're downstream consequences of the renderer path
switching. Regenerating the golden captures the current (correct) behavior.

## CP=4 vs TP=1 divergence on long prompts (2026-04-26)

Added a 4k-input smoke pair
(`v4_flash_4k_tp1_sm100` / `v4_flash_4k_cp4_ep4_sm100`) against a
~4228-token summarization prompt over `docs/dsv4/cuda13_2/runbook.md`.
TP=1 target passes; CP=4 target produces **different but coherent**
English.  Both complete exactly 50 tokens, both have identical
`prompt_tokens=4228`, neither crashes or NaN's.  Full content side-by-side:

| Config | First 50 generated tokens |
|--------|----------------------------|
| TP=1   | `To reproduce the CUDA 13.2 build and test locally, a developer must: 1) Pull the appropriate CUDA 13.2 dev image (ARM or x86) using pouch. 2) Start a dev container with GPU` |
| CP=4   | `This is an excellent, comprehensive guide for setting up a CUDA 13.2 development environment on Alibaba Cloud Linux 3 with NVIDIA GPUs. The document is well-structured and covers all the critical steps from host prerequisites to troubleshooting common failures.` |

Same checkpoint, same deterministic decoding (`top_k=1, temperature=0`).
The first-token argmax flips because ~60 layers of all-gather
reduction-order FP noise (rank-local Q × gathered-KV, compressor
gather-before-S-pool, indexer top-k ordering) accumulates past the
argmax boundary by the last prefill position's hidden state; the decode
path then follows a different but equally valid trajectory.

The short-prompt CP=4 smoke (`v4_flash_cp4_ep4_sm100`, 11 input tokens)
happens to land on the same argmax as TP=1 because padded attention at
that length is too simple for the noise to cross a decision boundary.

**Acceptable** — CP=4 output is valid natural language and reflects the
input correctly.  The `v4_flash_4k_cp4_ep4_sm100` target is left
commented out in `internal_source/rtp_llm/test/smoke/BUILD` until we
either (a) land a CP-specific golden, or (b) do a layer-by-layer
hidden-state comparison via `record_tensor` to quantify and, if
needed, fix the accumulated drift.

## Why a new image tree (not a patch to existing x86 cuda12_9)

(rhel8+): both nvcc and the runtime libs link against glibc 2.28
symbols. You cannot install `cuda-toolkit-13-2` on alios7 — the dnf

2. **Patch `base_gpu_cuda12_9.Dockerfile` with conditional installer
   paths.** Same problem: the FROM chain is still alios7.
3. **Start fresh from `hub.docker.alibaba-inc.com/ali/os:8u-v7`** like the
   ARM GB200 path does. ✅ Chosen. Self-contained, no shared state with
   legacy x86 images.

Result: `internal_source/cuda_x86_docker/` is a parallel directory to
`internal_source/cuda_arm_docker/` with x86-specific URLs and no
shared ancestry with `internal_source/package/`.

# DeepSeek V4 在 vLLM 中的 KV Cache 结构说明

本文档整理自对 `vllm-project/vllm`（含 DeepSeek V4 支持分支）中 KV cache 规格、分配、对齐与各算子读写路径的分析，便于后续维护或改造 allocator。

---

## 1. 有哪些 `KVCacheSpec`、在哪里返回

DeepSeek V4 路径上**具体子类**主要是两种：`MLAAttentionSpec` 与 `SlidingWindowMLASpec`（定义在 `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`）。

| Spec 类型 | 模块 / 位置 | 作用 |
|-----------|----------------|------|
| **`MLAAttentionSpec`** | `DeepseekV4MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`（`deepseek_v4_attention.py`） | `compress_ratio > 1` 时：**主路压缩后的 FP8 K**（`cache_dtype_str=fp8_ds_mla`、`model_version=deepseek_v4`、`alignment=576` 等）。`compress_ratio ≤ 1` 时返回 **`None`**（仅 SWA，不报独立压缩 K spec）。 |
| **`MLAAttentionSpec`** | `DeepseekV4IndexerCache.get_kv_cache_spec` | **Indexer 的 K cache**（`head_dim` 常为 132 维 byte 宽、`compress_ratio`、`alignment=576`；**不传** `cache_dtype_str`，走通用 `head_size × uint8` 的 `real_page_size_bytes`）。 |
| **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`** | `DeepseekV4SWACache.get_kv_cache_spec`（`sparse_swa.py`） | **SWA 的 paged K**（`block_size=64` 写死、`sliding_window=config.sliding_window`、`model_version=deepseek_v4`；**不传** `compress_ratio`，默认 **1**）。 |
| **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`** | `CompressorStateCache.get_kv_cache_spec`（`deepseek_compressor.py`） | **Compressor 中间 state**（fp32，`block_size` C4 为 **4**、C128 为 **8** 等）。 |

**注意**：C4 / C128 / SWA-only 的区分**不是**在 `DeepseekV4MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` 里写分支，而是每层实例的 **`self.compress_ratio`** 不同，同一构造代码即可。

### 框图：四条可分配 KV 规格的来源

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph MLA["MLAAttentionSpec"]
    A1["DeepseekV4MLAAttention<br/>仅当 compress_ratio 大于 1"]
    A2["DeepseekV4IndexerCache<br/>Indexer K"]
  end
```

## 2. 每层有几块 KV cache 区域（按 `get_kv_cache_spec` 计数）

vLLM 里「一块」指：**一个**在 `compilation_config.static_forward_context` 中注册、且 `AttentionLayerBase.get_kv_cache_spec` **返回非 `None`** 的条目；`attn_utils.get_kv_cache_spec` 只会把这些名字放进 allocator 用的 **`dict[layer_name, KVCacheSpec]`**（见 `v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py`）。

### 2.1 HF `compress_ratios` 在 vLLM 里怎么用

`model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py` 对每层（`layer_id < num_hidden_layers` 时）：

- `self.compress_ratio = max(1, config.compress_ratios[layer_id])`。  
- 因此 HF 里写的 **`0` 会变成 `1`**（注释说明与 MTP 等未列入 `compress_ratios` 的层对齐），**不会出现「ratio 为 0 的压缩层」**。

Indexer 仅在 **`compress_ratio == 4`** 时构造（C4A / sparse indexer 路径）：

```261:359:vllm/vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py
        # NOTE(zyongye) Compress ratio can't be 0
        # we do this for because MTP layer is not included
        # in the compress ratio list
        if layer_id < config.num_hidden_layers:
            self.compress_ratio = max(1, config.compress_ratios[layer_id])
        else:
            self.compress_ratio = 1
        ...
        self.indexer = None
        if self.compress_ratio == 4:

                topk_indices_buffer=topk_indices_buffer,
                compress_ratio=self.compress_ratio,
                prefix=f"{prefix}.indexer",

```

主路上的 **`DeepseekCompressor`**（写主压缩 K、带 `CompressorStateCache`）在 **`compress_ratio > 1`** 时挂在 `DeepseekV4MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper` 上；C4 层因此同时存在 **wrapper 侧 compressor** 与 **indexer 内 compressor**（两套 **state_cache**，`layer_name` 不同）。

### 2.2 按层类型的区域个数

| 层类型（vLLM 生效后的 `compress_ratio`） | 非空 `KVCacheSpec` 条数 | 对应模块（逻辑名，均在 `static_forward_context`） |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **`compress_ratio == 1`**（HF 原为 `0` 或 `1`） | **1** | 仅 **`DeepseekV4SWACache`**。`DeepseekV4MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` 返回 `None`，**无主压缩 K、无 compressor、无 indexer**。 |

| **`compress_ratio == 4`（C4）** | **5** | 上列 **3** 再加上：**Indexer K**（`DeepseekV4IndexerCache`）+ **indexer 内 `CompressorStateCache`**（与 wrapper 侧 state **两块独立 tensor / 独立 layer_name**）。 |

### 2.3 与两种官方 `config.json` 的对应关系

以下链接为 Hugging Face 上的 **`compress_ratios` / `sliding_window` 来源**（两模型 **`sliding_window` 均为 128**）：

- [DeepSeek-V4-Flash `config.json`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/blob/main/config.json)  
- [DeepSeek-V4-Pro `config.json`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/blob/main/config.json)

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash**：`compress_ratios` 以 **`[0, 0, 4, 128, …]`** 等形式给出 → 前两层在 vLLM 中为 **`max(1,0)=1`** → 每层 **1** 块 KV 区域（仅 SWA）；自第三层起在 **4** 与 **128** 间交替 → 每层分别为 **5** 块（C4）或 **3** 块（C128）。列表末尾若出现 **`0`**（如为 MTP 等预留），同样变为 **1** → 行为同 SWA-only（**1** 块）。

**DeepSeek-V4-Pro**：`compress_ratios` 以 **`[128, 128, 4, 128, …]`** 开头 → **最前两层即为 C128**（每层 **3** 块），其后仍按 **4 / 128** 交替为 **5** 或 **3** 块。`num_hidden_layers` 等与 Flash 不同，**具体每层仍以该层索引在 `compress_ratios` 中的取值（经 `max(1,·)`）为准**。

## 3. 几个容易混的数字

| 符号 | 含义 | 典型来源 |
|------|------|-----------|
| **`sliding_window`（如 128）** | SWA **注意力语义窗口**（能 attend 的 token 范围） | `config.json` → `config.sliding_window` |
| **`cache_config.block_size`（如 256）** | vLLM **KV 分页的逻辑块长**（token / block） | `CacheConfig`，与 HF `sliding_window` 无直接相等关系 |
| **`compress_ratio`（4 / 128）** | **时间压缩步长**（多少 token 合成一条压缩侧记录） | `config.compress_ratios[layer_id]` |
| **SWA `block_size=64`** | SWA **paged 张量**的块内 token 数（与 C4A 压缩 K 拼页相关） | `sparse_swa.py` 注释：`256//4` 等推导 |
| **584** | **DeepSeek V4 `fp8_ds_mla`** 下**每个压缩槽**的字节宽（448 NoPE + 128 RoPE + 8 scale） | `MLAAttentionSpec.real_page_size_bytes` |
| **576** | **`alignment`**：对**整页** `real_page_size_bytes` 做 `round_up(·, 576)`，满足 FlashMLA / 打包 | `_apply_alignment_padding` |

**C4 主压缩区页大小（概念）**：在 `block_size=256`、`compress_ratio=4` 时，`storage_block_size = 256/4 = 64`，未 padding 的 `real_page_size_bytes ≈ 64×584`，再经 **576 对齐**。

**C128 主压缩区**：`storage_block_size = 256/128 = 2`，`real_page_size_bytes ≈ 2×584`，与 C4 **天然不同**；若要与其它层**共分配 / HMA**，依赖 **`page_size_padded` 与 bucket 抬档**（见下节）。

## 5. HMA、多组 KV 与 padding

- **不同子模块**（主压缩 K、SWA、compressor state、indexer…）的 **`page_size_bytes`** 可能差很多。
- **若要共 raw / 同一套 layer tuple / bucket**：在 **`kv_cache_utils._get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_groups`** 等路径中，会把较小页的 **`page_size_padded`** 抬到 **full-MLA 组 `all_page_sizes` 中 ≥ 当前值的最小一档**（`size_to_candidate`）。
- **代价**：小页层可能 **padding 占比高**；换 **分池、不共 tensor** 可简化但增加 allocator 与碎片成本。

**576 vs 584**：**584** 是**每槽内容宽度**；**576** 是**整页字节**的 **round_up 步长**。顺序是：**先按布局算 `real_page_size_bytes` → 再 `round_up(..., 576)`**；HMA 的 **candidate** 一般来自**已走过对齐的 `page_size_bytes` 集合**，避免「抬档后破坏 576 栅格」。

## 6. `CompressorStateCache` 与 SWA

- **`CompressorStateCache`**：仅在 **`DeepseekCompressor`** 内构造；存 **compressor 的 fp32 kv/score**（`_save_partial_states_kernel`），再经 **`_fused_kernel`** 写 **主压缩 K**。与 **SWA cache** 不是同一数据：SWA 来自 **`fused_wqa_wkv` 的 kv** 经 norm/RoPE/量化插入；compressor 来自 **`fused_wkv_wgate`** 的另一套投影。
- **`overlap`（仅 C4）**：  
  - **`coff = 1 + overlap`**：加宽 **每 token** 的 kv/score 特征，**`state_dim = 2 * coff * head_dim`** 必须与线性层宽度一致。  
  - **`OVERLAP`（fused kernel）**：在压缩边界 **gather `(1+OVERLAP)×COMPRESS_RATIO` 个时间位置** 做 softmax 加权；C4 为 **8 个位置**（多叠前一个 4-token 块），C128 为 **128 个位置**、无叠块。

# DeepSeek V4 KV Cache 接入 RTP-LLM：`KVCacheManager` 架构建议

本文档把「在现有 **KVCacheManager → CacheConfig → KVCacheAllocator（如 HybridTypeKVCacheAllocator）→ KVCacheGroup → BlockPool** 链路上支持 DeepSeek V4 多路 KV」的设计建议落盘，便于评审与分阶段实现。

背景材料：

- vLLM 侧多路 spec 与块数归纳：同目录 [`deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md`](./deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md)
- 论文/技术报告：`DeepSeek_V4.pdf`（混合 CSA/HCA、百万上下文、KV 与算力等）

---

## 1. 目标与矛盾

### 1.1 DeepSeek V4（参考 vLLM 实现归纳）在 KV 上的特征

同一 **Transformer 层** 下，可能出现 **多条需独立分配/绑定的缓存**（最多约 **5 路**）：

| 区域（逻辑名） | 典型角色 |
|----------------|----------|
| 主压缩 MLA K | `compress_ratio > 1` 时的 FP8 压缩 K 等 |
| SWA paged K | 滑动窗口注意力用 K（与 HF `sliding_window` 语义相关） |
| Wrapper Compressor state | 主路 compressor 的 fp32 中间态 |
| Indexer K | 仅 **C4**（`compress_ratio == 4`）路径上的 indexer |
| Indexer 内 Compressor state | indexer 内独立 `CompressorStateCache`，与 wrapper 侧 **不同 layer_name** |

各路的 **dtype、每块字节数、`block_size` / 时间压缩步长** 可能不同；读写 kernel 对 **`slot_mapping` vs `block_table`** 的依赖也不相同（详见 `deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md` §7–8）。

### 1.2 RTP-LLM 当前能力

- `CacheConfig`：`std::vector<KVCacheSpecPtr>`、`layer_ids`、`group_types`、`linear_groups` / `full_groups`、`layer_to_group_id` 等，擅长 **按层归组** 与 **Hybrid：Full vs Linear** 混排。
- `HybridTypeKVCacheAllocator`：多 **`KVCacheGroup`**，每组对应一种 spec 与一套 malloc/match 策略。
- **全局 BlockPool + 按层/组地址换算**：擅长统一块调度与 PD 相关路径。

### 1.3 核心矛盾

V4 是 **「同逻辑层、多槽位、多布局」**；现有模型更贴近 **「一层（或一组层）↔ 一个 KVCacheSpec / 一个 Group」**。若强行塞进单一 spec，会在 **对齐、PD 拷贝、`blockCopy`** 上难以维护。

**落地路线**：**多 `group_id`、组间独立层数与 BlockPool、不做 padding、`layer_name` 暴露给 Python**（**§2**）；**各区域是否进 block cache / PD 分离**（**§3**）。

---

## 2. 建模策略（已选定）

### 决策摘要（评审结论）

采用 **多个 `group_id`** 承载 V4 多路 KV，并约定：

| 约束 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| **一「路」一组** | 每条需独立分配/绑定的缓存（主压缩 K、SWA、compressor state、indexer、**scale（`KVCacheScaleSpec`）** 等）对应 **独立 `group_id`**；其中 V4 主路与 SWA/compressor 用 **`MLAAttentionSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec`**（**§4**），**scale** 用 **`KVCacheScaleSpec`** 单独成组入池（**§8.1**）。 |
| **层数可不同** | 不同 `group_id` 可绑定 **不同数量的逻辑层**（例如 indexer 仅 C4 子集层存在）；`CacheConfig` 里各组的 `layer_ids` / 覆盖层集合 **不必对齐**。 |
| **BlockPool 独立** | 不同 `group_id` 使用 **各自的 BlockPool**（或等价：每组独立块调度与物理页），**不在组间做 stride / 页大小的 padding 对齐合并**。 |
| **禁止 padding** | 不采用「为对齐异构页而在池间填 padding / HMA 式抬档合并」等做法；**每池按自身 spec 紧凑分配**即可。 |
| **`seq_size_per_block` / `kernel_seq_size_per_block`** | **跨组**：**`seq_size_per_block` 目前各组一致**；**`kernel_seq_size_per_block` 可按组不同**（与 **§5** 块数换算一致）。 |
| **`layer_name` 为 Python 真源** | **`KVCacheManager`（或与其等价的 C++ 门面）维护 `layer_name → KV cache tensor` 映射**；**Python 侧模型仅通过 `layer_name` 取得对应 KV tensor**（与 vLLM 侧「按逻辑名绑 buffer」一致），避免 Python 硬编码 `group_id` 或全局层序。 |

实现上仍属前文「伪组」思路，但 **组间隔离**（层数、池、无 padding）与 **命名暴露** 已写死为产品约束。

## 3. 区域与路径：**block cache** 与 **PD 分离**

**本节为唯一权威说明**：各 KV **区域**是否进入 **block cache**、是否进入 **PD 分离**；后文只写 **「见 §3」**，不重复展开。

### 3.1 术语

- **block cache（及配套主路 / connector）**：参与 **块级保存**与 **reuse 复用**（`block_table`、块槽置换、主路 **`blockCopy`** 等），以及 **仅服务已进 block cache 的 KV** 的 **非 PD** connector（若产品定义）。**不进 block cache** ⇒ **不走**上述子系统、**不可按块 reuse**；tensor 仍可经各组 **BlockPool** 分配显存。
- **PD 分离**：prefill 与 decode 分离时的数据面；本方案包括 **`CacheStore`**、**`writeCacheStore`**、**P2P Connector**（同属 prefill→decode，可串接或并列，以实现为准）。
- **与 PD 无关的旁路（若有）**：其它 connector，与 **CacheStore / PD 分离** 解耦；配置须能区分，避免与 §3.2 混淆。

### 3.2 汇总表

下表为 **启用 PD** 时的路径约定；**未启用 PD** 时，**PD 分离** 一列所涉链路不启用，**主压缩 K / 满块 SWA / Indexer K** 等仍可仅依赖 **block cache** 与本地执行。

| 区域 | 进 **block cache（及配套主路 / connector）** | 进 **PD 分离** |
|------|-------------------|----------------|
| **主压缩 MLA K** | 是 | 是 |
| **SWA（已凑满、可分页）** | 是 | 是 |
| **SWA（尾部未满逻辑块）** | 否 | **必须** |
| **Wrapper / Indexer 内 compressor state**（未满块中间态） | 否 | **必须** |
| **Indexer K**（按块管理的 K，与主路一致） | 是 | 是 |

**说明**：**compressor state** 与 **SWA 未满** 语义见 §1.1；二者 **不进 block cache**，但 **必须** 走 **PD 分离**（**`CacheStore` / `writeCacheStore` / P2P Connector`**），以便 decode 续算。**Indexer 内 compressor state** 若同属未满中间态，与 **Wrapper compressor state** 同一格；若产品将某路改为全量可分页，再在配置中单列例外。

### 3.3 实现注意（仅此一处列举）

- **勿**将 **compressor state** 或 **SWA 未满** 挂入 **block cache** 或 **§3.1 所述 PD 无关旁路**。
- **勿**在启用 PD 时对其 **漏接** **`CacheStore` / `writeCacheStore` / P2P Connector**。
- **进 block cache** 的主 KV 与 **compressor / SWA 未满** 在 **协议字段与代码分支**上保持区分，避免 **`blockCopy` / `writeCacheStore`** 默认分支混绑。

## 4. `KVCacheSpec` 与内存布局

不建议把多路硬编码进单个「巨型 MLA spec + 子 offset」。**DeepSeek V4 主路与 SWA/compressor**：RTP-LLM 与 vLLM 使用 **`MLAAttentionSpec`**、**`SlidingWindowMLASpec`**（语义以 vLLM **`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`** 为真源；C++ **同名或一一移植**）。**`scale` 路**（非 vLLM 上表两类）：使用 RTP **`KVCacheScaleSpec`** **单独 `group_id` + 分池**（**§8.1**），**不**再保留独立 scale 区域。**是否进 block cache / PD** **见 §3**（`KVCacheScaleSpec` 路径按产品打标，与 **§3** 表一致即可）。

### 4.1 **`MLAAttentionSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec`** 与 V4 各区域

vLLM **V1** 将规格集中在 **`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`**（及 **`AttentionLayerBase.get_kv_cache_spec`**）。仓库内对 **DeepSeek V4 各模块返回何种 spec** 的逐条归纳见 **[`deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md` §1](./deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md)**（含 `compress_ratio` 与层上 **1 / 3 / 5** 块区域计数）。

**V4 路径：逻辑区域 → spec 类（与 vLLM 相同）**（与 `kv_cache_interface` 及 `deepseek_v4_kv_cache_analysis.md` 一致）：

| 逻辑区域 | **使用的 spec 类（与 vLLM 相同）** | vLLM 典型来源（`get_kv_cache_spec`） | RTP-LLM 说明 |
|----------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------|
| **主压缩 MLA K**（`compress_ratio > 1`） | **`MLAAttentionSpec`** | `DeepseekV4MLAAttention`（`cache_dtype_str=fp8_ds_mla`、`alignment=576` 等） | **直接**用 **`MLAAttentionSpec`** 实例（或 C++ 等价物），字段与 vLLM 一致；**`seq_size_per_block` / `kernel_seq_size_per_block`** 等与压缩槽换算 **照 vLLM**。`compress_ratio ≤ 1` 时 vLLM **可不报**该路，RTP **勿**再建主压缩 K 组。 |
| **Indexer K**（仅 C4） | **`MLAAttentionSpec`** | `DeepseekV4IndexerCache`（窄 `head_dim`、byte 宽等） | **另一 `group_id`**，仍为 **`MLAAttentionSpec`**，与主压缩 K **不同实例/不同 `layer_name`**，字段按 indexer 的 `get_kv_cache_spec` 填。 |
| **SWA paged K** | **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`** | `DeepseekV4SWACache`（`block_size=64`、`sliding_window` 等） | **直接**用 **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`**，与 vLLM 一致。 |
| **Compressor state**（wrapper / indexer 两套） | **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`** | `CompressorStateCache`（fp32，`block_size` 4/8 等） | **直接**用 **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`**；wrapper 与 indexer **各一 `group_id`**、**各一 spec 实例**，**禁止**改用 GQA/MHA 等异类 spec。 |

**小结**：**V4 与 vLLM 对齐的仅两种 spec 类** — **`MLAAttentionSpec`**、**`SlidingWindowMLASpec`**（上表）。**`scale` 路** 另用 RTP **`KVCacheScaleSpec`** **分组建池**（**§8.1**），**不**与上两类混名。差异仍体现在 **多 `group_id`、多实例、多 `layer_name`** 与 **§3** 路径打标。

**组间块参数（与 §2、§5 一致）**：**`seq_size_per_block` 各组一致**；**`kernel_seq_size_per_block` 可按组不同**。

`MemoryLayoutConfig`：若同一 **Transformer 层** 对应多路 buffer，通过 **多 `group_id` + 各组 tensor** 表达；**`KVCacheManager` 汇总 `layer_name → tensor`**，供 Python 绑定。**不做**单 tensor 硬拼接、**不做**跨组 padding 拼接。

## 5. Reuse 与块数语义

由 **`HybridTypeKVCacheAllocator`** 等按 **§4** 的 spec（**`MLAAttentionSpec` / `SlidingWindowMLASpec` / `KVCacheScaleSpec`** 等）与 **`group_id`** 落实。

### 5.1 **`match` 扫描方向**

| Spec 类 | **match** |
|---------|-----------|
| **`MLAAttentionSpec`**（主压缩 K、Indexer K） | **从左到右** |
| **`SlidingWindowMLASpec`**（SWA、compressor state） | **从右到左** |

**勿**跨类混用方向（例如对 SWA / compressor 使用 MLA 的从左到右）。

### 5.2 **Reuse 粒度、跨组块参数与分配侧语义**

- **Reuse**：只按 **`seq_size_per_block`**；**不含** **`compress_ratio`** 与压缩步长。是否参与 reuse / block cache **见 §3**。
- **跨组**：**`seq_size_per_block`** 各组一致；**`kernel_seq_size_per_block`** 可按组不同。**`MallocInfo`** 用统一逻辑 **`seq_len`**，各组内换算 kernel 块数。
- **分配 / kernel**（与 reuse 解耦）：主压缩 K 按 **压缩槽**（约 `ceil(seq / compress_ratio)`）；SWA / compressor 按 **per-token** 或 **per 原始块** 与各自 spec。

## 6. `KVCacheManager`、`CacheStore` 与 PD 实现要点

- **`layer_name → tensor`**：由 **`KVCacheManager`**（或 allocator 完成后注册）提供稳定键；Python **只按名取 tensor**；内部映射到 **`group_id` + BlockPool`**（对 **进 block cache** 的路，**§3**）。
- **RDMA / `regUserMr`**：每组独立池、不 padding 合并时，可按组或连续区注册 MR。
- **路径与 connector**：**block cache / PD 分离 / `CacheStore`** 的归属与边界 **仅 §3**；本节约束实现与 **`layer_name` / `group_id` 元数据**一致。

- **`BlockAddrInfo` / `BatchKVCacheResource`**：调度与传输策略 **遵循 §3**（block cache 与 PD 分离分列）。

# V4 gotchas — every non-obvious bug hit during bring-up

Sorted roughly by the order we'd hit them if bringing the model up on
a fresh machine. For every entry: symptom → root cause → fix.

## Environment / build

### 1. `stub_source -> open_source` breaks `cuda12_9_arm`

- **Symptom**: `bazel build --config=cuda12_9_arm //:th_transformer` fails
  linking `libtorch_cuda.so` against the CPU-only torch wheel.
- **Root cause**: `github-opensource/bazel/arch_select.bzl` is a symlink
  `→ stub_source/bazel/arch_select.bzl`. Default `stub_source →
  open_source` resolves to the open-source stub, whose
  `using_cuda12_arm` selector is `[]` → torch defaults to
  `torch_2.1_py310_cpu`.
- **Fix** (per worktree): 
  ```bash
  cd <worktree>/github-opensource
  rm -f stub_source && ln -s internal_source stub_source
  ```
  Memory-pinned as `worktree_stub_source.md`; do this immediately after
  every `git worktree add`.

### 2. torch wheel sha256 mismatch

- **Symptom**:
  `Error downloading torch-2.9.0+cu129-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl`
  `Checksum was XXX but wanted YYY`.
- **Root cause**: Alibaba PyPI mirror occasionally replaces the upstream
  wheel; repo-pinned sha goes stale.
- **Fix**: reuse a bazel cache that already successfully downloaded the
  old wheel:
  ```bash
  bazelisk --batch --output_user_root=/home/wangyin.yx/temp/bazel_bases/bazel_output_cursor build ...
  ```

### 3. Missing proto package markers

- **Symptom**: `ImportError: No module named rtp_llm.cpp.model_rpc.proto`
  when the backend tries to import `model_rpc_service_pb2`.
- **Root cause**: generated pb2 lives at `rtp_llm/cpp/model_rpc/proto/`
  but none of the intermediate packages had an `__init__.py`.
- **Fix**: committed three empty `__init__.py` files at
  `rtp_llm/cpp/`, `rtp_llm/cpp/model_rpc/`,
  `rtp_llm/cpp/model_rpc/proto/` (commit `55ecdccf3`). Still need the
  pre-existing pb2 generation step:
  ```bash
  bazel build //rtp_llm/cpp/model_rpc/proto:model_rpc_service_py_proto --config=cuda12_9_arm
  cp bazel-bin/.../model_rpc_service_pb2.py rtp_llm/cpp/model_rpc/proto/
  ```

## Model correctness

### 4. `precompute_freqs_cis` + meta + `to_empty` → all-zero RoPE

- **Symptom**: Model loads cleanly, all weights match, but generation
  output is pure gibberish token-soup.
- **Root cause**: `V4Transformer.__init__` is wrapped in
  `with torch.device("meta"):` to avoid blowing CPU RAM.
  `precompute_freqs_cis` creates a complex tensor from meta-device
  constants — stored via `register_buffer`. After `to_empty(cuda:0)`
  the buffer's shape survives but the values are reset to zero.
  `apply_rotary_emb` then multiplies by zero and RoPE is dead.
- **Fix**: `Attention.reset_rope_cache(device)` re-runs the
  precompute on the real device after materialize:
  ```python
  for layer in self.v4.layers:
      layer.attn.reset_rope_cache(device=device_str)
  ```
  Also clears the `freqs_cis` attr on compressor/indexer so they
  re-bind on next call.
- **Generalization**: any buffer with precomputed values is lost by
  `to_empty`. Explicit reset required post-materialize. Memory-pinned
  as `meta_tensor_to_empty_gotcha.md`.

### 5. Attention sink formula (sparse attn kernel)

- **Symptom**: Logit-space outputs technically finite but top-k
  decisions degenerate.
- **Root cause**: Initial impl folded `attn_sink` into the
  softmax-max term. Official TileLang `sparse_attn_kernel` adds sink
  to `sum_exp` **after** the softmax numerator accumulates.
- **Fix**: in `_sparse_attn` (`attention.py`),
  `sum_exp = sum_exp + exp(sink)` after the main reduction.

### 6. CSA prefill offset bug

- **Symptom**: prefill path produces different logits than the
  single-step decode path on the first decoded token.
- **Root cause**: `offset = kv_cache.size(1)` used for prefill; should
  be `offset = seqlen`.
- **Fix**: branch on `is_prefill` in `Attention.forward`.

### 7. FP4 packed-int8 vs FP8 dequant

- **Symptom**: routed-expert weights load as noise.
- **Root cause**: V4's routed experts are `float4_e2m1fn_x2` packed
  into `int8` (2 FP4 per byte) with UE8M0 block-32 scale, **not** FP8
  e4m3fn block-128 like the attention weights. Early loader used the
  FP8 dequant path for everything.
- **Fix**: `weight_loader.py` now branches on dtype — separate
  `_dequant_fp4_block32` (nibble-unpack low→even, high→odd, LUT
  `[0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0, -0.5, ...]`) and
  `_dequant_fp8_block128`.

### 8. Scale key derivation

- **Symptom**: `KeyError` loading routed-expert scales.
- **Root cause**: scale key is `base[:-7] + ".scale"` (strip `.weight`
  first), not `base + ".scale"`.
- **Fix**: corrected in `weight_loader.py`.

### 9. Scale and weight in different safetensors shards

- **Symptom**: ~10% of experts load with missing scales.
- **Root cause**: HF safetensors `weight_map.json` splits weight and
  its scale across different shards for some tensors.
- **Fix**: loader uses a lazy multi-shard `open_shards` cache, looks
  up every tensor through `weight_map` rather than assuming same-shard.

- **Symptom**: mHC / RMSNorm parameters built as bf16 instead of fp32
  → Sinkhorn numerical instability.
- **Root cause**: `set_default_dtype(bf16)` was too early, before the
  `nn.Parameter(dtype=fp32)` explicit-dtype parameters.
- **Fix**: set bf16 only around `V4Transformer(args)` construction,
  and explicit `dtype=fp32` parameters are unaffected.

### 11. `fastsafetensors` rejects F8_E8M0 scale dtype

- **Symptom**: backend dies on ckpt load with
  `RuntimeError: unsupported dtype F8_E8M0`.
- **Root cause**: V4 UE8M0 scales use a dtype the fastsafetensors
  library doesn't know about.
- **Workaround**: `--load_method scratch` (stock safetensors loader
  instead of fastsafetensors). Must be present in every invocation.

- **Symptom**: server init aborts trying to resolve an FMHA backend

- **Root cause**: stock `FMHAFactory` has no backend matching V4.
- **Fix**: `DeepSeekV4Model.prepare_fmha_impl` returns `None`. V4 runs

### 14. Mock per-layer KV cache (temporary)

- **Symptom**: framework-provided `kv_cache` arg into `forward` is
  ignored.
- **Root cause**: V4's CSA/HCA attention needs heterogeneous cache
  shapes per layer; the framework's `BlockPool` is single-spec.
- **Workaround (current)**: each `Attention` module keeps its own

### 15. OOM during model materialize when `--warm_up 0`

- **Symptom**: smoke test first attempt — backend SIGABRTs at
  `[DeepSeekV4Model] materializing on cuda:0` within 360 ms, never
  even reaches the ckpt loader.
- **Root cause**: `NormalEngine::NormalEngine()` calls `warmUp()`
  **before** `initCacheManager()` and `initExecutor()`. Skipping
  warm_up means `getKVCacheMemorySize` reads
  `getGpuExecStatus().device_memory_status.available_bytes` while the
  Python model is still on meta (no HBM allocated), sees ~180 GB free,
  reserves only the 5% / 2 GiB runtime floor, and hands ~180 GB to the
  KV pool. Then `initExecutor` runs, Python `initialize()` calls
  `to_empty(cuda:0)` which wants 150 GB — OOM.
- **Fix**: `--warm_up` default (1). Warm_up spins up a throw-away
  executor, materializes the model, runs a fake prefill, measures
  `max_used_memory`, releases. Subsequent `initCacheManager` uses
  `WarmUpResult.max_used_memory` as the runtime reservation, KV pool
  sized from the real residual. Other SM100 smoke cases set
  `--warm_up 0` because their models are small enough that the naive
  sizing naturally fits — V4 is the exception.
- Memory-pinned as `smoke_warmup_for_large_models.md`.

### 16. BF16 eager-dequant OOM path (historical)

- **Symptom**: early impl tried to convert FP4/FP8 → BF16 at load
  time. 149 GB disk footprint became ~600 GB RAM → dead.
- **Root cause**: natural to start with BF16-everywhere for ref-impl
  simplicity; forgot that dequant bloats memory 4×.
- **Fix**: `qlinear.py` keeps native FP4/FP8 dtypes as Parameters with
  separate UE8M0 scale Parameters; `linear()` fwd does per-call
  dequant to BF16 GEMM. Current path. Still leaves perf on the table

## DP + EP (S7c bring-up, 2026-04-26)

### 17. ACCL-EP intranode kernel rejects `num_topk=6`

- **Symptom**: all 4 ranks die during the first real-query forward with
  `RuntimeError: Failed: Assertion error
  .../ACCL-EP-.../csrc/kernels/intranode.cu:2237 'false and "Unsupported
  num_topk"'`. Warmup phase passes (no real MoE work).
- **Root cause**: ACCL-EP's `intranode_dispatch` has a compile-time
  `switch (num_topk)` that only covers `{2, 4, 8, 16}`. V4-Flash uses
  `n_activated_experts=6` (DeepSeek's own official model.py also
  uses 6). The default branch is the assertion.
- **Fix**: `moe.py::MoE._pad_topk_for_deepep` — before calling
  `buf.get_dispatch_layout` / `buf.dispatch`, pad `(indices, weights)`
  from 6 → 8 (next supported) by appending two slots of
  `(indices=-1, weights=0.0)`. The `-1` padding slots survive dispatch
  (recv_topk_idx matching loops skip them via
  `torch.where(... == expert_id)` never matching), and weight=0 means
  they contribute nothing even if they somehow did match.
- Do NOT try to patch the `.so` — it's a binary wheel. The pad
  approach adds ~2 extra topk slots of dispatch bandwidth, negligible.

### 18. ACCL-EP's `recv_topk_idx` is LOCAL, not global

- **Symptom**: DP+EP smoke passes warmup, passes `get_dispatch_layout`,
  passes `dispatch`, then produces zero output from every expert (no
  `torch.where(recv_topk_idx == expert_id)` ever matches anything).
  The resulting all-zero hidden state makes downstream layers blow up
  in weird places (`mhc.softmax` with "unknown parameter type",
  various NaN-propagating errors).
- **Root cause**: ACCL-EP's `dispatch` returns `recv_topk_idx` in the
  **local** expert index space — values in `[0, n_local_experts)` with
  `-1` for tokens whose topk choice for that slot didn't land on this
  rank. Upstream public DeepEP documents the output differently (some
  versions return global indices), but ACCL-EP returns local. The
  existing factory router `deepep_normal_router.py` explicitly shifts
  with `recv_topk_idx + self.rank_expert_offset` — the +offset is load-
  bearing.
- **Fix**: in `moe.py::_routed_experts_deepep` after `buf.dispatch`,
  shift local → global before the per-expert loop:
  ```python
  global_topk_idx = torch.where(
      recv_topk_idx == -1, recv_topk_idx,
      recv_topk_idx + self.local_expert_start,
  )
  ```
  Then the loop `for i in range(local_start, local_end):
  torch.where(global_topk_idx == i)` matches correctly.
- Also force `.to(torch.int64).contiguous()` on `recv_topk_idx` — the
  ACCL path sometimes hands back a non-standard dtype (observed as
  "unknown parameter type" on `torch.where(idx == i)` otherwise).

### 19. Empty-batch under DP desyncs DeepEP collective

- **Symptom**: rank with zero local tokens short-circuits the forward
  to a zero tensor for speed; other ranks enter `buf.dispatch` and
  block forever → `RuntimeError: DeepEP error: CPU recv timeout`.
- **Root cause**: DeepEP `get_dispatch_layout` + `dispatch` + `combine`
  are **collective** operations — all ranks must enter them together.
  Any rank that skips the layer stack deadlocks the buffer. Empty
  batch during DP (some ranks get 0 tokens when requests don't
  balance) naturally creates this divergence.
- **Fix**: don't short-circuit the forward on empty batch when
  `ep_size > 1`. Instead, at `DeepSeekV4Model.forward` pad `S_local==0`
  with a single dummy input_id (`torch.zeros((1,1), dtype=long)`) so
  every rank runs the full layer stack including the DeepEP collective.
  Discard the dummy's output slice (`hidden[:, :0]`) after forward.
  Note: V4's individual ops (rope, MHC softmax, indexer einsum) also
  had to be made empty-batch-safe anyway — see entries 20–22.

### 20. `apply_rotary_emb` crashes on empty `freqs_cis`

- **Symptom**: `RuntimeError: shape '[1, S, 1, 32]' is invalid for
  input of size 0` during warmup (framework probes prefill at
  max_seq_len then decode(1), which pushes `start_pos` past the end
  of V4's internal `freqs_cis` buffer → `freqs_cis[start_pos:start_pos+1]`
  is empty).
- **Root cause**: `apply_rotary_emb` does
  `freqs_cis.view(1, x.size(1), 1, x.size(-1))` — view of a 0-element
  tensor to non-zero shape.
- **Fix**: no-op on empty `x` or empty `freqs_cis` (DP rank with no
  local tokens, warmup OOB). Also replaced `unflatten(-1, (-1, 2))`
  with explicit `unflatten(-1, (x.size(-1) // 2, 2))` — some torch
  paths (dynamo/fakemode, certain warmup shapes) reject the `-1`
  inferred dim with "unknown parameter type".

### 21. Indexer einsum OOM at long context

- **Symptom**: `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to
  allocate 255.98 GiB` during warmup at max_seq_len=64K+.
- **Root cause**: `indexer.py` materializes a
  `[B, S, n_heads, T] fp32` intermediate (64K × 64 × 16K × 4 =
  256 GB) for the `einsum("bshd,btd->bsht", q, kv)` + relu + weight-
  sum. V4-official uses a TileLang `index_score_kernel` that fuses
  all three and skips the intermediate entirely.
- **Fix (stopgap, kept as fallback)**: S-dim chunking in `indexer.py`
  — pick `chunk_size` so peak `chunk_size * n_heads * T * 4 bytes` ≤
  2 GB, loop over chunks, concat. Keeps memory bounded at any seqlen.
- **Fix (current default, P0 in `prefill_opt/final_plan.md`)**: custom
  Triton kernel `dsv4/_indexer_score_triton.py:v4_indexer_score`
  streams the H dim and writes only `[B, S, T] fp32` (the topk score
  itself).  Eliminates the intermediate, ~2.3-4.9× faster than REF
  across V4-Flash shapes, and folds the causal mask into the kernel.
  Active by default; opt-out with `DSV4_INDEXER_FAST=0` (which falls
  back to the chunked stopgap).

### 22. `V4Args.max_seq_len` hard-capped at 4096

- **Symptom**: `shape '[1, 262143, 1, 32]' is invalid for input of
  size 131072` — freqs_cis ends up 4096 long no matter what
  `--max_seq_len` said.
- **Root cause**: `_args_from_model_config` in `deepseek_v4_model.py`
  had `max_seq_len=min(int(mc.max_seq_len) or 4096, 4096)` — the
  `min(..., 4096)` was a conservative early-dev default that got
  left in.
- **Fix**: removed the cap — honor whatever the framework passes.
  V4-Flash targets 1M context.

### 24. Mega MoE requires a DeepGEMM source patch (even on NVCC 13.2)

- **Symptom**: with `DSV4_USE_MEGA_MOE=1`, first forward crashes with
  `RuntimeError: Assertion error (deep_gemm/.../jit/compiler.hpp:228): false and "NVCC compilation failed"`.
  NVCC output:
  ```
  .../deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.cuh(35):
    error: floating-point template parameter is nonstandard
        float kActivationClamp,
  cannot determine which instance of function template
    "deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl" is intended
  ```
- **Root cause**: `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl` takes
  `float kActivationClamp` as a non-type template parameter of
  floating-point type (C++20 P1907R1).  **Both NVCC 12.9 AND 13.2
  reject this** even with `-std=c++20` / `DG_JIT_CPP_STANDARD=20`;
  minimal repro `template<float X> __global__ void k(){}` still fails
  on 13.2.78.  DeepGEMM's JIT-generated `kernel.cu` emits e.g.
  `0x1.4p+3f` (= `10.0f`) as the template arg, which NVCC's frontend
  rejects at parse time.  (The prior comment "unblocks on NVCC 13" in
  this gotcha was wrong — nvcc 13 also does not implement P1907R1.)
- **Fix**: patch DeepGEMM to use a `bool kHasActivationClamp` template
  gate + a runtime `float activation_clamp` kernel argument.  Patch
  lives at `3rdparty/deep_gemm/0002-mega-moe-runtime-activation-clamp.patch`
  and touches two files:
  - `deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.cuh`:
    replace `float kActivationClamp` template param with
    `bool kHasActivationClamp`, add `const float activation_clamp`
    runtime arg, rewrite the `if constexpr` clamp block to gate on
    `kHasActivationClamp` and read `activation_clamp` at runtime.
  - `csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.hpp`: replace
    `to_string(args.activation_clamp)` in the JIT template-arg
    codegen with a `"true"`/`"false"` literal (gated on `!= infinity`),
    and append `args.activation_clamp` to the `launch_kernel` pack.
  The DeepGEMM wheel has to be rebuilt with this patch (`setup.py
  bdist_wheel` from the source tree) and the resulting wheel either
  uploaded to OSS (point `deps/requirements_cuda12_arm.txt` at it) or
  dropped into the bazel extracted-wheel cache.
- The MoE Python path itself (`moe.py::_setup_mega_moe`,
  `_routed_experts_mega_moe`, weight-stacking / SF transforms / symm
  buffer registration) is unchanged and needs no adjustment — the
  patch is confined to the DeepGEMM kernel + JIT codegen.
- **Default**: `_mega_moe_enabled()` is now opt-out — whenever
  `_mega_moe_available()` holds (patched deep_gemm + torch≥2.9 +
  SM100+ + initialised process group of size > 1), the MoE forward
  takes the fused path automatically.  Set `DSV4_USE_MEGA_MOE=0` to
  force the pre-mega ACCL/DeepEP dispatch + per-expert fp8_fp4_gemm_nt
  loop (for A/B comparison or as a temporary escape hatch if the
  fused kernel misbehaves).  Any non-SM100 worker / single-rank /
  unpatched-deep_gemm environment keeps running the fallback path
  without any config change.

## S8 — Context Parallel (prefill)

### 25. CP rank-local Q needs global-position RoPE / causal mask

- **Symptom**: with `--cp_rotate_method ALL_GATHER --tp_size 4
  --dp_size 1 --ep_size 4`, early scaffold smoke output diverged from
  golden even though the compressor gather produced a correct full
  compressed KV on every rank.
- **Root cause**: after the framework's zigzag-split, each CP rank
  holds `chunk_length = padded_seq / cp_size` tokens scattered
  *through* the full sequence (zigzag → rank 0 gets the FIRST and
  LAST pair, rank 1 the second and second-to-last pair, etc.).  V4's
  `Attention.forward` / `Indexer.forward` originally applied RoPE via
  `freqs_cis[start_pos:start_pos + seqlen]` — `seqlen` was the rank-
  local `chunk_length`, so rotation angles corresponded to positions
  `[0, chunk_length)` instead of the token's real global position.
  The gathered KV (written from rank-local projections then all-
  gather-restored) carries the CORRECT global-position rotations
  (compressor gathers BEFORE the S-pool + RoPE).  Query/key angle
  mismatch destroys attention logits.  Similarly, the indexer's
  start-of-prefill causal mask used `seqlen` as the local bound,
  dropping valid global positions and admitting future keys.
- **Fix**: `rtp_llm/models_py/modules/dsv4/cp.py::build_cp_context`
  derives a per-forward `CPContext` from
  `cp_info.prefill_qkv_padding_mask` + `prefill_qkv_restore_indice`
  carrying
  - `global_positions[chunk_length] int64` — local idx → global pos
    (formula-based: even/odd pair indices from the zigzag layout);
  - `unpad_restore[seq_len_full] int64` — gathered-flat idx for each
    real token in global order (used to strip padding after gather).
  `V4Transformer.forward` builds the context once and propagates it to
  every layer's `attn / compressor / indexer` via `set_cp_ctx`.
  Attention applies RoPE on rank-local Q and KV with
  `freqs_cis.index_select(0, global_positions)`, then all-gathers KV
  across the CP (== TP) group and index-selects with `unpad_restore`
  to get the full stripped KV.  `_get_window_topk_idxs_cp` +
  `_get_compress_topk_idxs_cp` build the sliding / compressed topk
  ids against the full-KV layout using global positions.  Indexer
  mirrors: `cp_freqs_cis_local` for Q RoPE, compressed-KV end-pos set
  to `seq_len_full`, causal mask built from global positions.
- **TP/CP head-sharding interaction**: RTP-LLM's
  `ParallelismConfig::get_attn_tp_size()` returns **1** whenever
  `prefill_cp_config.is_enabled()` — the TP group is REPURPOSED as
  the CP group.  `_args_from_model_config` now uses this helper (not
  raw `tp_size`), so Attention's head-sharding path stays off under
  CP and `Attention.tp_size == 1` ⇒ no trailing all-reduce.  Raw
  `tp_size`/`tp_rank` still flow into `V4Transformer.set_cp_info` as
  `cp_size` / `cp_rank` for the gather layout.
- **MoE under CP+EP=4**: rank-local — DeepEP's dispatch receives the
  `chunk_length` slice naturally.  Padding tokens dispatch junk but
  their outputs are discarded by the framework's exit all-gather
  after `restore_indices[padding_mask==1]` strip.

### 26. PyWrappedModel CP exit-gather runs on decode too ⇒ Sampler narrow crash

- **Symptom**: prefill + first-token sampling succeed (`Paris` was
  being generated correctly); the second Sampler call (for the token
  produced by the FIRST decode step) aborts with
  `rtp_llm::Sampler::forward → at::Tensor::narrow → torchCheckFail`.
  Rank 0 SIGABRT within 1 ms of the decode forward returning.
- **Root cause**: `PyWrappedModel::forward` unconditionally runs
  `context_parallel_processor_->handleOutputs(hidden, inputs, cp_params)`
  whenever `enable_prefill_cp` is set, for prefill AND decode.  During
  a pure-decode batch, `handleInputs` only populates the `num_decode_stream`
  combo_tokens and leaves `prefill_qkv_padding_mask` / `prefill_qkv_restore_indice`
  EMPTY (`num_prefill_stream == 0` skips the fill loop).  `ZigZagProcessor::handleOutputs`
  then:
  ```cpp
  valid_indices     = torch::nonzero(padding_mask).squeeze(-1);   // []
  combined_indices  = restore_indice.index_select(0, valid_indices);  // []
  hidden_states     = all_hidden_t.index_select(0, combined_indices);  // [0, D]
  ```
  producing a 0-row hidden.  `callForwardPostLayers` then runs
  `logits = mm(hidden_[0, D], lm_head.t())` → `[0, vocab]`, and
  `Sampler::forward` does `inputs.logits.narrow(0, 0, 1)` which OOBs.
- **Fix**: in `PyWrappedModel::forward` gate the `handleOutputs`
  call on `has_context_request = (input_lengths.size(0) != sequence_lengths.size(0))`
  — only run the CP exit-gather when this batch actually contains a
  CP-split prefill stream.  Pure-decode batches skip the gather and
  pass hidden through unchanged.  Matches the standard
  prefill/decode gating used by `callForwardPostLayers` itself.
- This was latent for any CP model that supports decode; Qwen3-Next's
  CP path routes decode through a separate `cp_write_cache_store_impl`
  so the bug didn't surface there.

### 23. Warmup batch OOM-s shared-expert path at large context

- **Symptom**: `MemoryError: std::bad_alloc` in `fp8_gemm_nt` via
  `shared_experts.forward` at warmup with max_seq_len=64K.
- **Root cause**: the warmup's dummy prefill has batch =
  `max_generate_batch_size * max_seq_len` packed tokens, and shared
  experts run on the full batch (no EP-shard). 32 × 64K × 4096 × 2 B
  = 16 GB just for the activation, plus scale/FP8 quant intermediates
  → OOM.
- **Fix**: for smoke, cap `--max_generate_batch_size 1
  --max_context_batch_size 1 --concurrency_limit 1
  --reserver_runtime_mem_mb 32768` plus `--max_seq_len 8192` during
  bring-up. Real deployment needs either a smaller warmup shape or a
  chunked shared-expert forward for mega-batch prefill.

# V4 kernel audit — what's a workaround, what stays

Every numerical primitive used today by `rtp_llm/models_py/modules/dsv4/` is
one of three things:

- **REF** — pure PyTorch reference, intentionally slow but bit-correct. Will
  be replaced by a native kernel.
- **NATIVE** — already on a production kernel. Nothing to do.
- **BYPASSED** — the framework has a primitive for this, but V4 currently
  ignores it because the dsv4 path was written standalone.

The audit also flags which upstream kernel replaces each REF/BYPASSED item,
based on the actual installed `deep_gemm` package (inspected at
`/opt/conda310/bin/python -c "import deep_gemm; dir(deep_gemm)"`) and the
rtp-llm factory abstractions under `rtp_llm/models_py/modules/factory/`.

## The FP4 format gap

The factory's FP4 path is built around **modelopt_fp4** (NVFP4) weights:
per-group FP8 e4m3fn scale + FP32 global scale + per-tensor input scale.

V4-Flash ships a **different FP4 recipe**:

- Weight: packed int8 (2 FP4 per byte), layout `[out, in//2]`
- Scale: UE8M0 (`torch.float8_e8m0fnu`), block 32 along K, `[out, in//32]`
- No global scale, no input scale (activations quantize at forward time)

This is the DeepSeek-native recipe — the same one DeepGEMM's
`fp8_fp4_gemm_nt` and `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_*` kernels consume
directly. **Matches V4 without format conversion.** The existing
`CudaFp4GEMMLinear` / `CudaFp4EpNormalStrategy` don't apply; a new
`CudaFp4Ue8m0DeepGEMMLinear` and matching MoE executor/strategy are needed,
but the low-level kernel call is a one-liner.

3. **K4 (MoE expert for-loop)** — ✅ DONE via per-expert `fp8_fp4_gemm_nt`

## What V4 does not currently need

- No W4A8 (`cutlass_w4a8_moe.py`) — V4 is W4A8 in the sense the act is
  FP8 and weight is FP4, but the bit-layout + scale format differ. Keep

- No Hadamard rotation — V4 ships weights without the rotate; official

The V4 stack currently lives under `rtp_llm/models_py/modules/dsv4/` as a

**Goal**: `moe.py:MoE.forward` stops looping over experts; runs one

```
def forward(self, x, input_ids):
    flat = x.view(-1, D)
    weights, indices = self.gate(flat, input_ids.flatten())
    # (a) permute tokens into [expert0_tokens, expert1_tokens, ...]
    perm, counts, inv_perm = permute_by_expert(flat, indices)
    # (b) quant permuted input to FP8-UE8M0 once
    a_fp8, a_scale = per_token_cast_to_fp8_ue8m0(perm, block=128)

    #     w1: [E, inter_dim, D//2]  (packed FP4), s1: [E, inter_dim, D//32]
    #     w3, w2 analogous
    deep_gemm.m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous(
        (a_fp8, a_scale), (w13, s13), y13, counts)
    # (d) silu(gate)*up (clamped), then a second grouped GEMM for w2
    …
    # (e) un-permute + apply routing weights + add shared expert
```

## Parallelism design (4TP/4DP + 4EP)

### Interpretation of the target — two configurations, validated independently

**Config A (TP=4 + EP=4):** single node, 4 GPUs, one 4-way mesh.
Each rank holds 1/4 of the dense weights AND 1/4 of the 256 routed
experts (64/rank). Attention Q/O split across TP; routed experts split
across EP; shared expert TP-split along inter-dim. DeepEP dispatch/combine
for the MoE all-to-all.

**Config B (DP=4 + EP=4):** single node, 4 GPUs, "attention-DP /
expert-EP" layout (the one DeepSeek papers recommend for decode).
Each rank holds the **full dense weights replicated** — attention, LM head,
shared expert all run independently per rank. Only the routed experts
are sharded across EP=4 (64/rank). Before the MoE block, tokens dispatch
via DeepEP to the rank owning each selected expert; after, combine
back. No TP all-reduce inside attention. Higher memory footprint per
rank but removes attention-path communication — wins on decode latency.

These are **two separate smoke cases** (`v4_flash_tp4_ep4_sm100` and
`v4_flash_dp4_ep4_sm100`) each gated on TP=1 green.

### V4 shapes under TP=4

| Weight | Shape | TP split | Notes |
|--------|-------|----------|-------|
| `embed.weight` | `[129280, 4096]` | vocab-parallel along dim 0 (ParallelEmbedding) | or replicated; vocab split saves 32 GB×4 |
| `head.weight` (LM head) | `[129280, 4096]` fp32 | row-split, all-reduce at output | |
| `hc_head_fn` | `[hc, hc*dim]` | replicate (small, ~65 KB) | |
| Attention `wq_a` | `[1024, 4096]` fp8 | replicate OR TP-split along q_lora_rank | lora rank 1024 already small |
| Attention `wq_b` | `[64*512, 1024]` fp8 | **column-split heads**: 64/4=16 heads per rank | |
| Attention `wkv` | `[512, 4096]` fp8 | replicate — only 1 KV head (MQA) | cheap, `[512, 4096]` = 2 MB |
| Attention `wo_a` | `[8*1024, 64*512/8]` fp8 | split along groups (8/? groups per rank) | g=8, 2 groups/rank |
| Attention `wo_b` | `[4096, 8*1024]` fp8 | row-split, all-reduce | |
| Attention `attn_sink` | `[64]` | split — 16/rank | |
| Compressor `wkv / wgate` | fp32 small | replicate | |
| `Indexer.wq_b` | `[64*128, q_lora_rank]` fp8 | col-split heads: 16/rank | |
| Routed expert `w1/w2/w3` | `[inter=2048, 4096]` fp4 ×256 experts | **EP-split**: 64 experts/rank | stacked `[64, 2048, 2048]` |
| Shared expert `w1/w2/w3` | `[2048, 4096]` fp8 | TP-split along inter dim | 512 inter/rank |
| Gate `weight` | `[256, 4096]` fp32 | replicate | ~1 MB |
| Gate `bias` | `[256]` fp32 | replicate | |
| Gate `tid2eid` | `[V, 6]` int32 (hash layers) | replicate | |

Communication primitives needed per forward:

1. **Attention output**: after `wo_b` (row-split), `all_reduce` across TP
   group to sum partial sums. One AR per attention block.
2. **MoE dispatch**: after `gate` (replicated), tokens go to the rank that
   owns each expert via DeepEP `dispatch`. `combine` does the inverse.
3. **Shared expert output**: after `w2` (row-split), `all_reduce`. One AR
   per MoE block.
4. **LM head**: after `head` if row-split, `all_reduce` over vocab chunks
   (or gather).
5. **Embedding**: if vocab-parallel, `all_reduce` over partial results.

mHC residual: the stream is `[B, T, hc_mult, d]`. TP split is along the
last dim — all HC operators (`hc_pre / hc_post / hc_split_sinkhorn /
hc_head_reduce`) need a final `all_reduce` on the mixed stream since
they depend on `x_flat @ hc_fn`.

### The MQA-under-TP problem

V4 attention is **MQA with 1 KV head shared across 64 Q heads**. When
TP=4 splits Q heads 16/rank, the 1 KV head must be **replicated** on every
rank. This is cheap (`wkv` is `[512, 4096]` in fp8 = 2 MB) but requires
setting `kv_head=1, tp_kv=1` — the `tp_strategy` on `wkv` must be `sp_id`
(identity, no split), not the default `sp_head`.

The existing `deepseek_v2.py:MlaAttnAtomicWeight` handles this. Mirror
its `config=MlaConfig(...)` pattern when we write V4's weight info.

### Implementation sketch

1. Add `rank, world_size, tp_group, ep_group` to `V4Args`.
2. In `V4Transformer.__init__`, slice:
   - embed vocab: `local_vocab = ceil(V/world_size); embed = nn.Embedding(local_vocab, dim)`
   - each `Attention(...)` receives `n_heads // tp_size` and slices its Q/O linears
   - `MoE(...)` receives `[start_expert, end_expert)` slice of routed experts
3. In `Attention.forward`, after `wo_b`, call
   `dist.all_reduce(out, group=tp_group)`.
4. In `MoE.forward`, insert DeepEP `dispatch` before the expert compute
   and `combine` after.
5. Weight loader: instead of loading all experts into memory, filter by
   `[start_expert, end_expert)` and stream only the shards that contain
   them (multi-shard loader already supports lazy `_get_tensor`).
6. The hc residual stream stays `[B, T, hc, d_local]` where
   `d_local = d // tp_size`; `hc_fn` splits along its second dim and the
   `hc_split_sinkhorn` math runs locally with a single `all_reduce` on the
   resulting `mixes` term.
